title: URL Module
definition: A core module providing utilities for URL resolution and parsing. It breaks down a full web address into readable, manageable pieces.
simpleExplanation: If someone hands you `https://google.com:8080/search?q=cats&sort=new`, trying to manually split that string to find the search term is a nightmare. The URL module instantly dissects it into neat pieces: the protocol (https), hostname (google.com), port (8080), path (/search), and search parameters (q=cats).
realWorldExample: Reading the `?sort=desc&page=2` query parameters from an incoming request in a Node server so you know how to query your database.

basic: What global class is used in modern Node to parse URLs?
intermediate: How do you easily grab the value of `?user_id=123` from a URL?
advanced: Why is the old `url.parse()` method deprecated?

answers.question: What global class is used?
answers.answer: The `URL` class. It is available globally without needing to require the module, as it matches the standard Browser URL API.

answers.question: Why is url.parse() deprecated?
answers.answer: The old Node-specific `url.parse()` had security flaws (URL spoofing vulnerabilities) and didn't conform to the modern WHATWG web standard. The new `new URL()` global class solves this and works identically in both browsers and Node.
